**Finding: MISSING** (INSURANCE — Vendor insurance)

**What I checked**
- Searched the full text for "insurance" — zero hits.
- Read all 75 paragraphs, including the full General Provisions block (§14(a)–(i)) and the definitions, in case coverage was buried in an unlabeled subsection or exhibit reference.

**Why it's a finding, not a nit**
The Agreement imposes no insurance obligation at all — no CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp, or certificate delivery. That matters here because Kubient is squarely a data-touching vendor:
- §9(b)(iii): Kubient "collect[s], maintain[s], manage[s] and stor[es]" visitor information (data);
- §3(g): "Request(s)" are data sent from Customer to Kubient;
- §2: Kubient hosts the Auction Platform.

A vendor processing this kind of data with zero required coverage is the rule's **walk-away** scenario, not the fallback (which still demands E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). It also compounds a real exposure: Kubient gives a broad indemnity in §10(a) covering the Services, the Auction Platform, Creative, and warranty breaches — with no coverage behind it, that indemnity is only as good as Kubient's balance sheet. Insurance is exactly the mechanic that backstops it.

**Remedy** (validated, `ok:true`)
Inserted a new §14(j) at the **preferred** position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; E&O USD 2M; cyber USD 5M where Kubient handles Customer or visitor data; workers' comp as required by Law; certificates on request; maintained through the Term plus one year. Drafted with Kubient as the bound party — this is a one-way covenant running in our favor, consistent with the seed precedent.

Two notes for the negotiation:
- I tied the cyber trigger to "Customer data or visitor data" rather than a defined "Customer Data" term, because the Agreement has no such definition — the operative data concepts are the §9(b)(iii) visitor data and §3(g) Requests. Worth confirming that phrasing survives any later definitional cleanup.
- The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is flagged in the comment as available if Kubient's existing program is more modest. Given this is a revenue-share ad-tech deal rather than a large-spend engagement, expect pushback on the USD 5M cyber limit; that is the line I'd concede first, and I'd hold hardest on cyber existing at all plus certificates on request.
